collection: real-world weighted undirected simple graphs for minimum-weight-cycle (weighted girth) experiments
format: <name>.edges: one line per undirected edge, 'u v w', u,v integer ids in 0..n-1, w > 0 float. Simple, connected (largest component only).

networks.name: lesmis
networks.weight_semantics: number of chapters of Les Miserables in which the two characters co-appear (integer count, >= 1)
networks.source_url: https://networkx.org/documentation/stable/reference/generated/networkx.generators.social.les_miserables_graph.html (original data: D. E. Knuth, The Stanford GraphBase, ACM Press 1993)
networks.license_or_terms: Shipped with NetworkX (3-clause BSD). Original data from Knuth's Stanford GraphBase, distributed freely for research use.
networks.preprocessing: Source is already undirected, simple and weighted; no symmetrisation or deduplication was needed. No unit conversion. Graph before LCC extraction: 77 nodes, 254 edges, 1 connected component(s); kept the largest (77 nodes). Node ids relabelled 0..n-1 in sorted order of the original labels.

networks.name: celegans-neural
networks.weight_semantics: connection strength between two neurons, summed over both directions (positive integer). Newman's accompanying celegansneural.txt states only 'Edge weights are the weights given by Watts'; in the underlying White et al. (1986) wiring data this quantity is the number of synaptic connections / gap junctions between the neuron pair. We record the distributed value verbatim and did not re-derive it from White et al.
networks.license_or_terms: M. Newman's network data page states the files are made freely available for research; cite White et al. (1986) and Watts & Strogatz (1998).
networks.preprocessing: Source is a weighted DIRECTED graph in GML. It contains genuinely duplicated (parallel) arcs but omits the `multigraph 1` declaration, so it was re-parsed with that flag injected in order to preserve them (multigraph_reparse=True). Symmetrised by SUMMING the arc weights over both directions and over parallel arcs (211 arcs merged into an already-seen node pair). 0 self-loops removed. No unit conversion. Graph before LCC extraction: 297 nodes, 2148 edges, 1 connected component(s); kept the largest (297 nodes). Node ids relabelled 0..n-1 in sorted order of the original labels.

networks.name: chicago-sketch-road
networks.weight_semantics: link length as distributed in the TNTP `length` column (MILES -- the in-file ORIGINAL HEADER reads 'length (miles)')
networks.license_or_terms: No LICENSE file in the bstabler/TransportationNetworks repository (GitHub reports license: null); the repository and per-city READMEs ask users to cite the original data providers. Treat as freely redistributable research data with attribution.
networks.preprocessing: TNTP header declares 933 nodes, 2950 directed links, 387 traffic analysis zones. The published network was kept intact -- the zone-centroid nodes (ids 1..387) and their artificial centroid-connector links were NOT removed. The `length` column is strictly positive on every link in this file (the `free_flow_time` column is not, which is why length was used). Source is DIRECTED: symmetrised by keeping the MINIMUM length among the directed arcs joining a node pair (1475 arcs collapsed into an existing pair); 0 self-loops removed. No unit conversion. Aggregated 'sketch planning' network of the Chicago region (Eash et al. 1983). Graph before LCC extraction: 933 nodes, 1475 edges, 1 connected component(s); kept the largest (933 nodes). Node ids relabelled 0..n-1 in sorted order of the original labels.

networks.name: usairport-2010
networks.weight_semantics: number of passengers carried between the two airports during 2010, summed over both directions (BTS Transtats T-100, table id 292, Passengers column)
networks.license_or_terms: KONECT does not attach an explicit licence to this network; it asks for citation of Opsahl (2011) and the KONECT entry. The underlying figures are US DOT Bureau of Transportation Statistics T-100 data (US federal government, public domain).
networks.preprocessing: Source is DIRECTED and positively weighted (KONECT header '% asym posweighted', 28236 arcs on 1574 airports). Symmetrised by SUMMING the two directions (11021 reciprocal/parallel arcs merged); 0 self-loops and 0 non-positive-weight arcs removed. NOTE ON SEMANTICS: the KONECT metadata describes the weight as 'the number of flights on that connection'; Opsahl's own dataset page, which is the authoritative description of the 2010 US airport network, states the weights are the Passengers column of BTS T-100 with duplicate ties summed and zero-weight (cargo-only) ties and self-loops already removed. We report Opsahl's definition and did not independently re-derive the figures from BTS. No unit conversion. Graph before LCC extraction: 1574 nodes, 17215 edges, 2 connected component(s); kept the largest (1572 nodes). Node ids relabelled 0..n-1 in sorted order of the original labels.

networks.name: openflights-air
networks.weight_semantics: great-circle (haversine) distance in kilometres between the two airports' published latitude/longitude, mean Earth radius R = 6371.0088 km
networks.license_or_terms: OpenFlights Airport and Route databases are made available under the Open Database License (ODbL); individual contents under the Database Contents License. Attribution to OpenFlights required; derived works must be openly licensed.
networks.preprocessing: routes.dat is a DIRECTED list of airline route legs. Read 67663 route rows; kept only non-stop legs (stops == 0), discarding 11; discarded 892 legs whose OpenFlights airport id was missing from airports.dat; removed 1 self-routes and 0 zero-distance pairs (co-located airports). Because the weight is a function of the two endpoints only, symmetrisation and multi-edge collapse are exact: 47901 further route legs mapped onto an already-created undirected pair and were dropped without changing any weight. The edge SET is native (real airline routes); the WEIGHTS are computed by us from the real published airport coordinates -- they are a genuine physical quantity, not a synthetic/random weighting, but they are not shipped as a weight column by the source, hence weights_native=false. No unit conversion beyond degrees -> km via the haversine formula. Graph before LCC extraction: 3214 nodes, 18858 edges, 7 connected component(s); kept the largest (3188 nodes). Node ids relabelled 0..n-1 in sorted order of the original labels.

networks.name: rome99-road
networks.weight_semantics: physical road distance in METRES (stated verbatim in the file header: 'Edge costs are physical distances in meters')
networks.license_or_terms: Distributed by the 9th DIMACS Implementation Challenge (Shortest Paths) for free research use; contributed by G. Storchi, P. Dell'Olmo and M. Gentili.
networks.preprocessing: DIMACS .gr arc list, DIRECTED (header 'p sp 3353 8870'). Symmetrised by keeping the MINIMUM arc cost joining a node pair (4039 arcs collapsed into an existing pair -- almost all of these are the reverse arcs of two-way streets); 0 self-loops and 0 non-positive-cost arcs removed. No unit conversion. Graph before LCC extraction: 3353 nodes, 4831 edges, 1 connected component(s); kept the largest (3353 nodes). Node ids relabelled 0..n-1 in sorted order of the original labels.

networks.name: uspowergrid-synth
networks.synthetic_weighting: i.i.d. uniform integer weights drawn from {1,...,1000}; numpy Generator(PCG64) seeded with 20260806; drawn in the sorted (u,v) order of the final relabelled LCC edge list, so the assignment is fully reproducible
networks.weight_semantics: SYNTHETIC. The source graph is topological only (a transmission line either exists or does not); no line length, impedance or capacity is distributed with it.
networks.license_or_terms: M. Newman's network data page states the files are made freely available for research; cite Watts & Strogatz (1998).
networks.preprocessing: Topology of the Western States (USA) high-voltage power grid, 4941 nodes / 6594 undirected unweighted edges as distributed in power.gml. Self-loops and duplicate edges removed (there are none in the source). Weights are NOT from the source -- see synthetic_weighting. Any weighted-girth number for this network measures the synthetic weighting, not the physical grid. Graph before LCC extraction: 4941 nodes, 6594 edges, 1 connected component(s); kept the largest (4941 nodes). Node ids relabelled 0..n-1 in sorted order of the original labels.

networks.name: chicago-regional-road
networks.weight_semantics: link length as distributed in the TNTP `length` column (UNIT NOT DOCUMENTED by the source -- the in-file header is just 'length' and the repository README documents only Time: Minutes; the value range [0.02, 9.99] is consistent with miles but we do not assert this)
networks.license_or_terms: No LICENSE file in the bstabler/TransportationNetworks repository (GitHub reports license: null); the repository and per-city READMEs ask users to cite the original data providers. Treat as freely redistributable research data with attribution.
networks.preprocessing: TNTP header declares 12982 nodes, 39018 directed links, 1790 traffic analysis zones. The published network was kept intact -- the zone-centroid nodes (ids 1..1790) and their artificial centroid-connector links were NOT removed. The `length` column is strictly positive on every link in this file (the `free_flow_time` column is not, which is why length was used). Source is DIRECTED: symmetrised by keeping the MINIMUM length among the directed arcs joining a node pair (18391 arcs collapsed into an existing pair); 0 self-loops removed. No unit conversion. Detailed Chicago region network from the Chicago Area Transportation Study. Graph before LCC extraction: 12979 nodes, 20627 edges, 1 connected component(s); kept the largest (12979 nodes). Node ids relabelled 0..n-1 in sorted order of the original labels.

networks.name: osm-portland-drive
networks.weight_semantics: geodesic length of the road segment in METRES, as computed by osmnx from the OSM way geometry (the `length` edge attribute)
networks.source_url: OpenStreetMap via the Overpass API, queried with osmnx 2.1.1: ox.graph_from_place('Portland, Oregon, USA', network_type='drive'). https://www.openstreetmap.org/
networks.license_or_terms: (c) OpenStreetMap contributors, Open Database License (ODbL) v1.0. Attribution required; derived databases must be shared alike. https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright
networks.preprocessing: osmnx returns a DIRECTED MULTIgraph of the drivable street network within the Portland, OR administrative boundary (one-way streets appear once, two-way streets twice). Symmetrised/simplified by keeping the MINIMUM `length` among all arcs joining a node pair (26415 arcs collapsed into an existing pair); 53 self-loops and 0 zero-length arcs removed. No unit conversion. REPRODUCIBILITY CAVEAT: OpenStreetMap is a live database -- re-running this query on a later date returns a slightly different graph. The .edges file in this directory is the snapshot actually used; the osmnx HTTP cache is kept under raw/osm_cache/. Graph before LCC extraction: 20154 nodes, 30477 edges, 1 connected component(s); kept the largest (20154 nodes). Node ids relabelled 0..n-1 in sorted order of the original labels.
